method: Source-backed ecological dossiers. Operational suggestions are author interpretations; no universal perfect-condition or catch model is asserted.

species.name: Lingcod
species.region_scope: California coast; local precision varies by source

claims.claim: Rocky habitat and vegetation with prey support an adult search; ledges and crevices have a seasonal spawning role. Juvenile sandy habitat cannot be substituted for the adult target.
claims.confidence: Moderate for broad habitat context; local catch rate uncalibrated
claims.geographic_transfer: Check the original geography, life stage and method before applying elsewhere.

species.map_policy: Local relief, rough cover and connected habitat support a sounder search. Large mapped relief is not a boulder measurement or proof of higher catch rate.
species.depth_strategy: Keep the current 200-foot ceiling. Deeper rocky edges can be a later, separately qualified comparison; there is no demonstrated local catch advantage from 250 or 300 feet alone.
species.conditions_use: Comfort and gear control are scored separately. Tide height does not supply bottom-current speed. Missing wave, wind or current evidence is not a favorable condition.
next_measurements: Bottom contact and drift observed on the boat
Dated catch and effort by depth, including empty drifts

species.map_policy: Keep rocky candidates and inspect the water column with sonar. Split ecological models by identified species before fitting a catch relationship.
species.depth_strategy: A deeper band may change species composition and handling demands. Depth is not a universal quality score; retain the user limit until a separate rollout is requested.
species.conditions_use: Comfort and gear control are scored separately. Tide height does not supply bottom-current speed. Missing wave, wind or current evidence is not a favorable condition.

species.region_scope: California coast; local precision varies by source

claims.claim: California halibut use soft-bottom inner-shelf and estuarine habitat. CDFW describes most angler catches in shallow water; this does not establish a universal optimum at every port.
claims.confidence: Moderate for broad habitat context; local catch rate uncalibrated

species.map_policy: Show connected, fully depth-screened sediment areas and preserve holes. A sand/reef boundary is a search lead, not a catch claim.
species.depth_strategy: The existing 100-foot habitat selection is an app planning cutoff. Automatically extending to 300 feet is not justified by the reviewed recreational evidence.

species.name: Chinook salmon
species.region_scope: California coast; local precision varies by source

claims.claim: Migratory ocean fish follow changing prey and ocean conditions. NOAA reports anchovies dominating Central Coast ocean-caught Chinook diets in 2020–2021; that dated finding does not locate a current school.
claims.confidence: Moderate for broad habitat context; local catch rate uncalibrated
claims.geographic_transfer: Check the original geography, life stage and method before applying elsewhere.

species.map_policy: Show coastal water-column search references, updated legal access and dated forage/catch context. Do not attach a salmon school to a reef pin or a juvenile survival index.
species.depth_strategy: Water-column presentation depth and seafloor depth are different. Use observed bait/fish depth and lawful gear; a 300-foot seabed limit is not an ocean salmon optimum.
species.conditions_use: Comfort and gear control are scored separately. Tide height does not supply bottom-current speed. Missing wave, wind or current evidence is not a favorable condition.

species.region_scope: California coast; local precision varies by source

claims.claim: Ocean temperature and frontal structure influence albacore distribution. NOAA describes broad migrations; a suitable water mass does not establish fish presence.

species.depth_strategy: Bottom depth does not define pelagic access. Offshore distance, fuel reserve, return sea state and actual school depth constrain this boat more directly.

species.region_scope: California coast; local precision varies by source

claims.claim: Pacific bluefin occupy a broad range and migrate over large distances. Feeding, body size and depth behavior make a single fixed surface-temperature optimum inappropriate.

species.name: Dungeness crab
species.life_stage: Legal-sized adults; larval and nursery evidence separate
species.region_scope: California coast; local precision varies by source

claims.claim: CDFW quality sampling uses depth strings at 90, 150–180 and 210–240 feet. Those are sampling strata, not proof that the deepest stratum maximizes recreational catch.
claims.confidence: Moderate for broad habitat context; local catch rate uncalibrated
claims.geographic_transfer: Check the original geography, life stage and method before applying elsewhere.

species.map_policy: Show connected soft-bottom areas and separate gear/season/whale-risk permission. The reported unsuccessful shallow trip and otter explanation are a local hypothesis to test, not a fitted depth rule.
species.depth_strategy: A legal, comparable 210–240-foot trial would be a more evidence-linked future experiment than assuming 300 feet is best. Keep published fishing targets within 200 feet until expansion is authorized and gear/depth/closure screens are complete.
species.conditions_use: Comfort and gear control are scored separately. Tide height does not supply bottom-current speed. Missing wave, wind or current evidence is not a favorable condition.
